Compelling real-world case studies demonstrating practical improvements (40% power gain in scDRS, 10.5% enrichment in pgBoost) and novel biological discoveries

Incomplete information: code repository URL appears broken (marked with dot); some optimization prompts not fully documented; cannot compare with concurrent work due to unavailable code

strengths: Addresses well-motivated problem of accelerating scientific method development
Comprehensive evaluation on 11 established benchmarks with proper methodology (train/val/test splits, multiple seeds, ablations)
Demonstrates concrete improvements in baseline benchmarks (average rank 1.2 for single-cell tasks) and shows real impact on genetics methods (scDRS power improvement 40%, pgBoost enrichment +10.5%)
Thorough ablation studies validating contribution of each component (Table 3)
Transparency in experimental details, prompts, and code templates; honest reporting across different LLM backbones
Integration of domain knowledge from scientific literature is sensible and shows strongest ablation effect
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: knowledge tree structure, draft-then-refine strategy, and Bayesian category sampling are established techniques; core innovation is engineering integration rather than fundamental methodological contribution

Significant fairness concerns in experimental comparison: AIDE crashes on >50% tasks with 8hr timeout, Biomni/ChatGPT-Agent have 1hr limits while TusoAI gets 8hrs, deep learning baselines use 'best of 10 one-shot models' not iterative optimization, different LLM backends across baselines; key experiment missing: AIDE with 8hrs and proper configuration

Attribution problem: ablations show domain knowledge drives most improvement (0.20 gap), raising question whether specialized architectural choices (Bayesian updates, diagnostics) matter substantially compared to simpler alternatives using same knowledge

Unvalidated biological claims: 9 novel autoimmune-T cell associations and 7 variant-gene links lack independent validation in external datasets, experimental validation, false discovery rate analysis, or mechanism discussion—presented as discoveries but are unvalidated predictions

Limited scope and questionable generalization: evaluation restricted to single-cell bioinformatics and small NASBENCH-360 deep learning tasks; no evaluation on truly novel scientific problems; selection criteria for benchmarks (>1 dataset, fast runtime) exclude harder problems; unclear transferability to other domains

Code diversity measurement concerns: TF-IDF is crude syntactic metric; CodeBERT abandoned because >0.997 similarity (suspicious, suggests metric validity issues); unclear if diversity is semantically meaningful

Performance inconsistencies: Decomposition shows 0.07-0.64 variance across runs (contradicts claimed <0.01 CIs); negligible improvements on some tasks (Label, Visual both 0.89/0.44 for both expert and TusoAI); test performance sometimes notably lower than validation, suggesting overfitting
Hyperparameter choices lack justification: time limits, α=0.8 probability, 1.1 Bayesian update factor appear arbitrary; no sensitivity analysis
Knowledge gathering limitations: only top 10 papers by citation count with no quality filtering; limited to 1200 words of methods sections; may miss recent innovations or domain-specific advances

Case studies are narrow: scDRS and pgBoost optimizations target specific components (scoring functions, distance features) rather than full method development—closer to parameter tuning than novel discovery

strengths: Clear problem motivation addressing a real bottleneck in scientific method development with concrete examples from genetics
Thoughtfully designed system integrating domain knowledge via structured knowledge trees with hierarchical planning and Bayesian updates
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 11 diverse scientific tasks with multiple strong baselines (AIDE, Biomni, ChatGPT-Agent) and thorough ablations
Consistent improvements across benchmarks (average rank 1.2 for single-cell, 2.8 for deep learning) with 16% average improvement in single-cell tasks
Real-world impact demonstrated through case studies showing 40% power improvement for scDRS, 10.5% enrichment improvement for pgBoost, and discovery of novel biological associations
Generated methods are novel (not simple implementations), computationally efficient, and interpretable with clear insights (e.g., log-log transformation)
Strong reproducibility practices including extensive supplementary material, prompt templates, and promised code release
Analysis of code diversity showing TusoAI explores substantially more diverse solutions than AIDE baseline
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—core contributions are primarily in system integration (knowledge tree is structured prompting, Bayesian updates are simple multiplications, diagnostics are standard feedback). Novelty is in engineering rather than algorithmic innovation

Baseline comparison concerns: AIDE was designed for workflow construction not component optimization; deep learning comparisons use best-of-10 random attempts instead of iterative agents; concurrent work (Aygun et al. 2025) cannot be compared; no classical AutoML baselines tested

Evaluation design issues: validation-set choice sensitivity unexplored; improvements sometimes marginal (e.g., 0.89 vs 0.89 on Label task, <1% on some deep learning tasks); modest statistical improvements relative to confidence interval widths in some cases

Knowledge tree construction underspecified: no sensitivity analysis for initial categories, paper selection, or predefined diagnostic category design; 'draft-then-refine' strategy not justified against alternatives

Unclear generalization: only 11 tasks tested (single-cell cluster in genomics); domain transfer to chemistry, physics, materials science not explored; artificial constraint of optimizing only tuso_model function limits real-world applicability

Missing critical analyses: no time-sensitivity analysis beyond 8 hours; cost-benefit analysis absent (costs vary from $0.24 to $22.3); error rates and failure modes not quantified; knowledge ablation granularity insufficient (removes all vs. some)

Results sensitive to LLM choice (Table 3) with instability across models; only one open-source model tested; no analysis of why reasoning models sometimes underperform; LLM stochasticity and library dependencies affect reproducibility

Warm-start advantage not isolated: case studies start from expert methods (scDRS, pgBoost); ablation separating cold-start vs. warm-start contributions missing, potentially inflating improvement claims
Biological validation concerns: novel discoveries in Section 5 lack independent expert validation; claims about 'novel biology' not verified in peer-reviewed biology literature
Incomplete ablations: no exploration of alternative categorization schemes; feedback mechanism variants not tested; ablation on number of papers selected not provided

Strong case studies demonstrating real biological impact with quantifiable improvements (21% more cell-disease associations, 13.8% higher eQTL enrichment) and validated discoveries
Thorough ablation studies systematically evaluating contribution of each component (knowledge trees, Bayesian updates, diagnostics, domain knowledge)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive appendices containing prompts, setup details, hyperparameters, and code release promised
Well-motivated problem addressing genuine bottleneck in computational method development with clear practical importance
Sensible system design integrating domain knowledge, iterative optimization with Bayesian updates, and diagnostic feedback for scientific discovery
weaknesses: Baseline fairness concerns: Biomni/ChatGPT-Agent limited to 1 hour/iteration while TusoAI has 8 hours; AIDE crashed when timeout extended—makes performance claims somewhat unfair

Limited core technical novelty: Knowledge trees are standard structured representations; Bayesian update (1.1× multiplier) is simplistic and unjustified; main contribution is architectural combination rather than algorithmic innovation
Case studies are warm-start only (optimizing existing methods scDRS/pgBoost), not developing methods from scratch—limits evidence for discovering truly novel approaches
Ablation study O contradicts core claims: domain knowledge importance appears modest (0 vs 10 vs 50 papers show similar performance), undermining the stated importance of literature integration

Methodological questions: arbitrary time/bug-fix limits (10 min, 4 fixes); diversity selection criterion (0.1%) lacks justification; heuristic choices throughout (code similarity clustering, 'most promising' selection)

Evaluation scope: only 2 case studies despite 11 benchmarks; deep learning tasks use small NASBench-360 datasets; generalizability to other scientific domains unclear; primarily biological focus
Unclear component importance: ambiguity about which components are essential (ablation results sometimes contradictory); causality between code diversity and performance not established
Incomplete baseline comparisons: concurrent work (Aygun et al. 2025) addressing similar problem cannot be directly compared; distinction from MLE agents could be clearer
System limitations: only operates on single functions; requires separate validation set; cannot modify evaluation procedures; LLM API dependencies and version specificity limit reproducibility

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap in scientific method development by integrating LLMs with structured domain knowledge
Comprehensive evaluation across 11 diverse tasks with extensive ablations and multiple LLM backbone tests
Real-world scientific impact demonstrated through case studies (scDRS and pgBoost improvements with novel biological discoveries)
Strong reproducibility with released code, detailed implementation, and prompt templates
Generated methods are genuinely novel rather than re-implementations of existing approaches
Thoughtful system design separating instruction-based and diagnostic-based optimization paths
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (knowledge trees, draft-then-refine, Bayesian updates) are established; main contribution is straightforward combination of existing techniques
Critical fairness concern with AIDE comparison: default 1-hour timeout fundamentally limits evaluation of the main ML engineering baseline; authors unable to increase timeout without crashes

Non-equivalent baseline comparisons: Biomni and ChatGPT-Agent evaluated non-iteratively due to web interface constraints; cannot compare with most similar concurrent work (Aygun et al. 2025) due to code unavailability
Knowledge tree construction lacks transparency: heavy reliance on LLMs to generate categories/instructions with no analysis of quality or sensitivity to initial instructions
Generalization concerns: focus heavily on computational biology (acknowledged); only 11 tasks with unclear applicability to other scientific domains
Incomplete ablations: missing ablations on Bayesian update rule (why 1.1×?), instruction vs. diagnostic split (80/20), and knowledge tree structure itself
Statistical analysis: single-cell CIs not shown ('all under 0.01'), only 3 random seeds, no formal significance testing; some individual improvements are modest
Computational cost inadequately addressed: 8-hour budget with variable costs ($0.24-$22.30), environmental footprint not discussed, may bias toward simpler methods
Validation design constraints may bias results: requirement for quick-running validation datasets may favor certain method types

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine bottleneck in scientific method development; existing systems focus on data analysis or general ML without domain-specific integration

Thoughtful system design with three key innovations: (1) knowledge tree for structured domain knowledge, (2) hierarchical planning with Bayesian utility updates, (3) diagnostic-based optimization pathway

Comprehensive evaluation: 11 tasks with consistent outperformance (avg rank 1.2 for single-cell, 2.8 for deep learning); strong baselines including AIDE (MLE agent), Biomni, ChatGPT-Agent, and expert methods

Demonstrated real scientific impact beyond benchmarks: scDRS improvements (40% power increase, 21% more true associations) uncovered 9 new T cell-disease associations; pgBoost improvements (13.8% enrichment) discovered 7 novel variant-gene links validated against literature
Excellent reproducibility: detailed experimental setups, complete prompt templates, runtime analysis showing efficiency, code diversity analysis (TusoAI vs AIDE), and stability across replicates
Strong ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating contribution of each component; code diversity analysis revealing TusoAI explores solution space more thoroughly than AIDE
Practical robustness: works across multiple LLMs (GPT-4o-mini to GPT-5); interestingly, cheaper models sometimes outperform expensive ones; includes warm-start capability for existing methods
Clear presentation with informative visualizations; Algorithm 1 clearly specified; extensive appendices providing transparency and supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for design choices: Bayesian update rule (πc ← 1.1πc) appears heuristic without principled justification for the multiplicative factor or adaptive alternatives

Significant applicability constraints: requires single-function optimization (fails on scattered codebases), needs separate validation experiment, vulnerable to weak evaluation functions, cannot optimize data selection or evaluation procedures themselves

Baseline comparison concerns: Biomni/ChatGPT-Agent were designed for data analysis (not method development), making comparisons somewhat unfair; deep learning baselines receive only 10 non-iterative attempts vs TusoAI's 8-hour iteration; missing direct comparison with concurrent Aygun et al. (2025) work
Domain coverage limited despite generality claims: all 6 single-cell tasks are biology, 4 of 5 deep learning tasks have biological applications; generalization beyond biology undemonstrated

Case study design raises questions about discovery vs. refinement: scDRS optimization targets region where scDRS has 'lower power' (task-specific tuning); pgBoost instructions explicitly guide toward distance-based features (guided refinement rather than autonomous discovery)

Statistical rigor concerns: some reported improvements are marginal (Table 2: TusoAI 0.70 vs Expert 0.69); no formal significance testing; knowledge source limited to top 10 citation-ranked papers (may miss recent specialized work)

Reproducibility of LLM components: multiple stochastic elements in instruction generation; generated instructions often generic across tasks (Appendix C shows repeated patterns); limited sensitivity analysis to prompt engineering

Missing failure analysis: insufficient discussion of task types/domains where TusoAI struggles; no analysis of when domain knowledge might be misleading; no examination of ill-specified evaluation function effects

Novelty of discovered methods somewhat overstated: many are combinations of known techniques (preprocessing, loss functions, ensembling); Appendix H's novelty defense sometimes just distinguishes from prior work rather than proving fundamental innovation
